title: Len Johnson: Site revealed for Manchester boxing statue

input.lead: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
input.summary: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
input.evidence_text: Len Johnson: Site revealed for Manchester boxing statue - BBC News Image source, Getty Image caption, Leonard Benker Johnson was one of the best boxers of his generation By Christian Brooks and Georgie Docker , North West Published 55 minutes ago He was one of Britain's best boxers, but never became champion. Born in Clayton, Manchester, in 1902, Len Johnson won more than 90 fights during his career but was barred from contesting the British title because of the colour of his skin. He later channelled the fighting spirit he showed in the ring into campaigning against racism, becoming a trade unionist, civil rights activist and member of the Communist Party. More than 50 years after his death, Johnson is set to become the first black person to be honoured with a statue in Manchester. But who was Len Johnson? Despite having little boxing knowledge or training, he got his first taste of the sport after a fight at work prompted his father, a former boxer, to take him to a local contest. A few weeks later, after training by skipping with an old washing line, he stepped into the ring for his first bout at the Alhambra Theatre in Openshaw. Johnson came out on top, beating fellow teenager Jerry Hogan with a third-round knockout. It marked the start of a career that would bring more than 90 victories. Image source, Getty Image caption, Johnson was the eldest of four siblings and was born on 22 October 1902 to a father from Sierra Leone and a mother from Ireland. Johnson's breakthrough came in 1925 when he defeated reigning British middleweight champion Roland Todd twice in seven months. title: Car driver who dragged head teacher to his death guilty of murder

input.lead: Simon Richardson is convicted of murdering head teacher Michael Mullins and will be sentenced on Monday
input.summary: Simon Richardson is convicted of murdering head teacher Michael Mullins and will be sentenced on Monday
input.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A man has been found guilty of murdering a head teacher who was dragged to his death for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car Simon Richardson crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was cycling home from his job at Stretford Grammar School on the evening of 20 April in the village of Warburton in Trafford, Greater Manchester Prosecutors claimed Richardson, 35, fled the scene of the crash before stopping to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist and then driving on with Mr Mullins still lodged underneath the vehicle Richardson was also convicted of dangerous driving and will return to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court to be sentenced on Monday There were shouts of "Yes!" from the court's public gallery as the guilty murder verdict was announced

title: Manchester United Munich air disaster memorial items stolen

input.lead: The foundation has urged the return of stolen items, saying they mean so much to bereaved families
input.summary: The foundation has urged the return of stolen items, saying they mean so much to bereaved families
input.evidence_text: Manchester United Munich air disaster memorial items stolen - BBC News Image source, Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation Image caption, The glass display case at Manchesterplatz, which has been fixed, contains memorabilia and tributes commemorating the Munich air disaster By Haider Saleem North West Published 30 October 2026 A glass sculpture and medals have been stolen from a memorial to the 23 people killed in the Munich air disaster, including eight Manchester United players. The items were taken from a display case at Manchesterplatz in Munich, where the plane crashed on take-off on 6 February 1958 after refuelling on its return from a European Cup match in Belgrade. Munich Police said the glass case around the memorial was smashed with a rock when the items were taken between 08:00 and 13:00 local time on Monday 26 October. The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF) said it was "deeply saddened", while its chair, Ifty Ahmed, said the theft had caused emotional harm to families. Image source, Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation Image caption, The memorial foundation said the glass was repaired on the same day, but some memorabilia remains missing Image source, Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation Image caption, The foundation's chair has said it was still unclear exactly how many medals were missing "They don't understand the damage that they've caused," Ahmed told BBC News. He said the memorial had provided solace for families who lost loved ones in the crash. "And whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories," he said. Image source, Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation Image caption, Ifty Ahmed (second left) has urged those responsible to return the stolen items, saying they mean so much to Manchester United supporte

title: Mums of autistic girls create special app for parents

input.lead: Kate Dunn and Nisha Warburton wanted to enable parents to connect and feel less isolated
input.summary: Kate Dunn and Nisha Warburton wanted to enable parents to connect and feel less isolated
input.evidence_text: Two mothers who created an app to help parents of children with special needs connect hope it means no one will feel alone Kate Dunn, whose daughter Ophelia has non-verbal autism and ADHD, met the mother of Sophia, also diagnosed with autism, Nisha Warburton, in a carpark outside their specialist nursery in Bolton, Greater Manchester Nisha said: "You go from feeling like the only person who is dealing with such a situation to recognising that actually a lot of people are." In their free time, or while their children were asleep, the pair decided to make the app, called SEN2gether, to create a community as well as to share information and tools for parents With almost 2,000 sign-ups within its first month, the pair have created a growing private community of parents and carers where they can share what works, ask questions as well as find local connections and guidance "We are just mums. We do not have a background in business or digital app making but what we notice is people love it and recognise it, and we are growing and developing it everyday," Nisha said

input.summary: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are among Chester pumpkin carver Jamie Jones' creations

title: Sixty police officers recruited for new Bee Network unit

input.lead: Some 60 more officers will be deployed across Manchester's Bee Network to make travel safer
input.summary: Some 60 more officers will be deployed across Manchester's Bee Network to make travel safer
input.evidence_text: Sixty police officer have been recruited to patrol Greater Manchester's trams and buses The new Transport Policing and Crime Command has been created to tackle crime and antisocial behaviour on the Bee Network The new squad will deliver a "significant increase" in visible policing and enforcement across the transport network, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The dedicated unit, which will also cover the city's active travel routes and roads, has been formed with funding from the Mayor of Greater Manchester's budget It will be supported by control centre staff at GMP and Transport for Greater Manchester, which has access to CCTV cameras across bus stations, interchanges, tram stops and train stations Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said the aim was to "make the roads and public transport among the safest in the UK"

input.summary: Hasaan Arshad breached security rules by transferring material from a GCHQ computer system in 2022
input.evidence_text: A GCHQ intern who was jailed for endangering national security by taking top secret data home has lost a bid to reduce his jail term Manchester University computer science student Hasaan Arshad breached tight security rules when he used his mobile phone to remove material from a computer system at GCHQ and transfer it to his private computer on 24 August 2022 The 26-year-old was jailed for seven-and-a-half years after he admitted an offence under the Computer Misuse Act and two charges of making an indecent photograph of a child On Thursday Lady Justice Cockerill refused Arshad permission to challenge his sentence, saying there were no arguable grounds that the sentencing judge was wrong 'I was not living a normal life, I was surviving' Published 1 day ago Home Guard training documents discovered in attic

The driver of the car, the court heard, was performing a 'creeping manoeuvre' to exit a service road near shops running adjacent t Coroner Julie Mitchell said the BMW 'crept out' and 'breached' the junction as parked cars impeded the driver's view. The views of both the driver and Mr Wadsworth would have been 'impeded' at the time, Ms Mitchell added The court heard a range of traffic calming measures have been implemented on Partington Street since the tragedy. input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia

input.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

input.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
input.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
